clue.text: A pectoral cross for ruler

indicators.note: cross here means angry or put out, so the letters of the words before it are worked up into a new order

explanation.surface: A churchman's breast cross is offered as an emblem for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pectoral cross' reads as a bishop's chest ornament, but 'cross' is the anagram signal working on A PECTORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Egyptian queen was a sovereign, so she is an example of a ruler.

clue.text: Small carriage carrying pop group to Savoy?

indicators.note: carrying means the carriage letters hold the pop group inside

parts.note: CGE is an abbreviation of carriage
ABBA is the Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: A little coach takes a pop band to the Savoy hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Savoy' suggests the London hotel, but the question mark points to the Savoy, a crinkly-leaved variety of the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Savoy is a variety of the leafy vegetable, so it is an example of the answer, as the question mark signals.

clue.text: For example, Greek leader with small type of pencil copied ovoid

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: leader points to the opening letter of Greek

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
H marks a hard pencil lead
aped means imitated or copied

explanation.surface: A Greek chief with a little pencil mimicked something oval.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid means like an egg in form, oval with one end broader than the other.

clue.text: "God is tripartite" corrected conjuror

indicators.note: corrected means the letters of the quoted phrase are put right, set in a new order

explanation.surface: A theological claim about the Trinity is put right by a magician.
explanation.definitionFit: A prestidigitator is someone skilled at sleight of hand, a performing magician.

clue.text: Briefly run away on short tryst maybe returning with youngster

indicators.note: returning means the combined letters are read backwards, as on a return trip
briefly means the word for running away loses its last letter

parts.note: to elope is to run away to marry

indicators.note: short means the meeting word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a date is one kind of tryst, a lovers' meeting

explanation.surface: A couple quickly steal away for a hurried romantic meeting, then come back with a child.
explanation.walkthrough: ELOP (ELOPE cut by 'Briefly') and DAT (DATE made 'short') join, and 'returning' reverses ELOPDAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the young of a frog or toad, so a youngster in the animal world.

clue.text: Increase in tension after African Union captures American agents

indicators.note: captures means the union letters take in the agents next to them
after means the tension letter follows the rest

parts.note: G-men are FBI agents in American slang
T stands for tension in physics

explanation.surface: Tension rises after an African body detains US agents.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to make larger or add to, a synonym of increase.

clue.text: Unspoken agreement a citizen conceals

indicators.note: the phrase agreement a citizen keeps the wanted letters tucked out of sight across its word breaks

explanation.surface: A deal is struck without words, kept quiet by a member of the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is understood or implied without being said, a direct synonym of unspoken.

clue.text: Hard-nosed veteran involved in foolish thug's boast about ducks

indicators.note: involved in means the veteran word is mixed up among the other letters
foolish means the letters of thug's boast and the ducks are scrambled, set out in a silly order
about here adds to the sense of letters being knocked around, with the ducks thrown into the mix

parts.note: old can mean experienced or long-serving, so veteran
the possessive is no letter, so thug's gives thugs
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so two ducks give two Os

explanation.surface: An old soldier gets caught up in a lout's bragging about ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the veteran sits whole in the middle of the scramble rather than being mixed in; a duck is a cricket score of nothing, hence the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone very resilient and unsentimental, which is what hard-nosed means.

clue.text: Horse runs about after snake

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
A is an abbreviation for about, as in approximately

explanation.surface: A horse bolts round in a panic after spotting a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The cobra is a venomous hooded serpent, an example of a snake.

clue.text: Locks Hitler's bodyguards in boxes?

indicators.note: in means the bodyguards' letters go inside the word for boxes

parts.note: box is a kind of shrub or tree, so boxes are trees
the SS began as Hitler's personal guard

explanation.surface: A dictator's guards are shut away in crates, under lock and key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like containers but means box trees; 'Locks' is hair, not fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tresses are long locks of hair, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Elder Dumbledore maybe an egotist

parts.note: an elder sibling is a big brother or big sister, so elder gives big
Dumbledore is the head of Hogwarts in the Harry Potter books, an example of a headmaster or head

explanation.surface: The older Dumbledore brother might be thought a vain show-off.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Dumbledore's elder brother; instead 'Elder' is the big of a big brother and Dumbledore, as headmaster, is a head.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceited, self-important person is called a swollen-headed type, so the word is a synonym for egotist.

clue.text: Break down with new leader and complain

indicators.note: a new leader means the word for break down gets a different first letter, its C becoming G

parts.note: to crumble is to break down into fragments

explanation.surface: Someone falls apart under a fresh boss and starts to moan.
explanation.walkthrough: The replacement G is not clued by any word; the setter simply swaps the first letter, which the answer confirms.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble is to moan or grouse about something, a straightforward synonym of complain.

clue.text: Dish made from wood, elm and teak primarily

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber, so a wood

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letter of each of elm and teak

explanation.surface: A serving plate is crafted from various timbers, chiefly elm and teak.
explanation.walkthrough: ASHET is a Scottish and northern English word for a large serving plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashet is a large oval serving plate, especially in Scotland, so a type of dish.

clue.text: Catches character briefly grabbed by balls

indicators.note: grabbed by means the shortened word is held within the cricket word

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, so balls stand for overs

indicators.note: briefly means the word for character is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: heart can mean a person's essential nature or character

explanation.surface: A fielder takes a catch after a player is seized by a run of deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, so 'balls' stands for overs; 'character' as a person's heart or nature is what gets docked.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a remark is to hear it, often by chance, which is what eavesdropping on someone means.

clue.text: Suitable old stamp's found in exercise books

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife, so old

indicators.note: found in means the stamp word sits inside the exercise and books letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
a die is a tool that stamps a design on coins or paper

explanation.surface: An antique postage stamp turns up in some school exercise books.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'stamp's' is 'is', a link before 'found in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedient means convenient or advantageous for a purpose, a close synonym of suitable.

clue.text: Falls leaving lake for reservoirs

indicators.note: leaving means the lake letter departs from the word for falls

parts.note: slumps are sudden falls or drops
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Waterfalls abandon a lake in favour of man-made reservoirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like waterfalls, the setting for lakes and reservoirs, but it means slumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is a pit or well where liquid collects, such as an oil reservoir in an engine.

clue.text: Aims — often broken!

indicators.note: broken means the letters of aims and often are smashed up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A wry dig that political pledges are routinely abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a party's published aims, which are often broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a published statement of a party's policies and goals, so it sets out its aims.

clue.text: A French drudge oddly never having seen a spade?

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of drudge

explanation.surface: A French labourer, strangely, has never set eyes on a shovel.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: ground never touched by a spade has not been dug.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth that no spade has worked is not excavated, so the playful description fits it.

clue.text: Open in advance without a break

definitions.meaning: candid and frank, saying things directly
two words meaning beforehand, as with payment, written as one with no gap between them

explanation.surface: Something is opened early and runs continuously.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is the two-word phrase meaning beforehand, run together with no space: 'without a break'.
explanation.definitionFit: The single word means frank or candid, and the phrase means paid beforehand, before the work is done.

clue.text: News stories of revolutionary father in old hospital

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning right round, so everything from father to hospital is read backwards
in means the father word goes inside the word for old

parts.note: senile means aged and failing, so old
da is an informal word for father
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Papers report on a rebel dad held in an aged infirmary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' sounds like a political rebel, but it turns the whole of the father-in-old-hospital assembly back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Headlines are the main items of the news, so they stand for the leading news stories.

clue.text: Possibly smacks prostitutes

definitions.meaning: a smack is a small fishing vessel, and Irish fishing boats of a similar type carry this name
a slang term for sex workers

explanation.walkthrough: 'smacks' looks like blows but means fishing boats; in Ireland a hooker is a traditional sailing fishing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hookers are both a kind of fishing boat, like smacks, and slang for prostitutes.

clue.text: One week with foster child possibly is difficult

parts.note: a means one, as in a dog
a ward is a child in someone's guardianship, such as a foster child

explanation.surface: Taking in a foster child for a week can be hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward means hard to deal with or tricky, a synonym of difficult.

clue.text: Brutes assisted in revolt after European departs

indicators.note: in revolt means the remaining letters rise up and are thrown into disorder
departs means the European letter leaves the word assisted

explanation.surface: Thugs helped in an uprising once a European had left.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing E from ASSISTED leaves ASSISTD, which 'in revolt' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadists take pleasure in cruelty, so they are brutes.

clue.text: Weapon fashioned from hard stick

parts.note: flint is a very hard stone, so as hard as flint
to lock is to jam or become stuck, so stick

explanation.surface: A weapon has been carved out of a tough length of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned from' looks like an anagram signal but is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flintlock is an old type of gun fired by a flint striking steel, so a weapon.

clue.text: Seizure in cardiac tissue unsettles surgeon initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the five words from in to surgeon

explanation.surface: A fit in heart tissue first rattles the surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' that looks like a link is the first of the five words whose opening letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Ictus is a medical term for a sudden attack, such as a stroke or fit.

clue.text: Split condition included in offer

indicators.note: included in means the condition word sits inside the offer word

parts.note: a bid is an offer, as at auction
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A proviso is written into a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bifid is a botanical term for something divided into two parts by a cleft, so split.

clue.text: Overcharge teetotaller in support group

parts.note: O for over and C for charge give OC, as in OC for officer commanding, the one in charge

indicators.note: in means the teetotaller letters go inside the support word

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
TT is short for teetotal, so a teetotaller

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't drink is overcharged at a support group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overcharge' looks like one verb, but splits into O (over) and C (charge).
explanation.definitionFit: An octette is a set of eight performers or things, so a kind of group.

clue.text: Inspires a body of scientists to cross river

indicators.note: to cross means the scientists' letters straddle the river, going either side of it

parts.note: RS is the Royal Society, the UK's academy of scientists
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A learned society is spurred on to bridge a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse feelings or interest is to stir or awaken them, close in sense to inspires.

clue.text: Stunner is more gentle after a change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart means the central letter of the gentler word is swapped, M becoming S

parts.note: tamer means more docile, so more gentle

explanation.surface: A beauty becomes milder once she has had a change of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' suggests a beauty; it is a weapon that stuns.
explanation.definitionFit: A taser is an electric weapon that immobilises a target, literally something that stuns.

clue.text: Penniless Swiss hoped for employment in fairground attractions

indicators.note: employment means the letters are put to work in a different arrangement
penniless means without a penny, and P is the abbreviation for penny, so P is removed from hoped

explanation.surface: A broke Swiss man hoped for a job among the fairground stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penniless' drops the P (penny) from HOPED, leaving HOED; 'for employment' then rearranges SWISS and HOED.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideshows are the small booths and amusements alongside the main show at a fair.
